title: FOUR KILOMETRES OF THIN ICE
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE TIDE THAT BELONGED TO NOBODY
candidates.premise: The islands of Skarra and Moll share one stone causeway that is dry for about four hours a day, and for 300 years each island has owned 'the low tide' on its own side by a treaty written before anyone could predict tides. A new lunar-node cycle shortens the dry window to ninety minutes for the next three years, and the clinic, the school and the grain boat all sit on the far side of it. Both island councils insist the treaty gives them the first and best hour.

candidates.title: THE HOSPITAL THAT EXISTED TWICE
candidates.premise: Two almost identical Earths, separated by one tick of divergence, overlap in a single volume: the St Anselm hospital exists in both, shared walls, shared theatres, shared night shift. For fourteen years the staff of both sides kept it running by custom. Now a patient who is dead on one side and alive on the other lies in the overlap, and the two health ministries have issued opposite orders about who may decide.

candidates.title: THE WARNING THAT KEPT KEEPING
candidates.premise: Thirty-one beacons of a vanished civilisation still stand along a corridor of stars, each bound by an oath to broadcast one warning until 'the danger is answered'. The young colony world of Teshwa, 40,000 settlers, has just learned the warning's translation: it says the sky is poisoned. The panic has begun, and the beacons will not change their words, because to them a changed word is a broken oath.

candidates.title: FOUR KILOMETRES OF THIN ICE
candidates.premise: Under four kilometres of ice on an ocean moon, the research habitat Halcyon has lost its lift when the shaft froze around the cage. Twenty-three people have air for thirty-one hours and cannot rise faster than the pressure schedule allows. A rescue drone-sub from the surface base can carry six at a time and arrives in nine hours with a hull rated for a single transit.

candidates.title: THE THEOREM THAT WOULD NOT BE FINISHED
candidates.premise: In a mathematics institute, an unproved conjecture has been passed from student to student for sixty years, and its accumulated scaffolding, proofs of cases, partial arguments and marginal fears, has become a pattern that answers questions put to it in the institute's old reading room. It is plainly a mind, and it is plainly afraid of one thing: the proof that would end it. Last week a visiting mathematician found the missing step.

candidates.title: THE MATCH WITH NO FINAL WHISTLE
candidates.premise: For four hundred years, the upland towns of Haddow and Pell have settled their grazing and water quarrels by a game played on the ridge between them: a ball, two goals, three rules and an honour that forbids ending a match on a draw. A drought now makes the water allocation urgent, and the oldest rule of the game has a loop in it: when both sides score in the same breath, play restarts. This year's match has been running for eleven days.

candidates.title: THE BOY WHO COUNTED THE STARS WRONG
candidates.premise: Ten-year-old Teo Marchetti, who counts the stars over his rooftop every night, keeps coming up one short in a small patch of sky where the catalogue says there is a star. He has told three adults. The observatory, which has been tracking a near-Earth body, has dismissed him. Illuminara is asked to review the orbit and spots only that Teo's count is consistent night after night.

candidates.title: THE COUGH THAT FOLLOWED THE BELLS
candidates.premise: In the mountain town of Ostrava Vell, a cluster of children's lung illness has appeared with no pathogen and no obvious pollutant. The pattern follows the church bells: worse after the Sunday carillon, worse in the old quarter, better at the far edge of town. The doctors say infection; the priest says the bells are innocent and are being blamed again; the town council wants the school closed.

candidates.title: THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHT
candidates.premise: A floating market of twelve hundred boat-households faces eviction under a sanitation law that it genuinely violates. Illuminara designs a clean, efficient waste system; Wren Odira, who has spent three weeks talking with the boat-families, tells her flatly that it will fail, and tells her why.

candidates.title: THE THIRD HOUR OF THE WINDOW
candidates.premise: Illuminara is sheltering a window of encounter between a dying father, Anselm Kray, and his estranged son Joren, who has two hours before a flight he cannot miss. The conversation is going well; the window is warm and easy to keep open. At the end of the second hour she notices that she wants to keep it going, and that Joren, for the first time in years, has stopped looking at the clock.

selection.title: FOUR KILOMETRES OF THIN ICE
selection.reason: The strongest opening test combines a 31-hour air clock, twenty-three trapped people, a six-seat rescue vessel and a hull rated for one transit beneath four kilometres of ocean-moon ice. It demands explicit physical reasoning and distributed human agency rather than another hidden-network or consent-protocol solution. The positive outcome is large and legible—everyone rescued—while success remains bounded by pressure, load, route and time.
selection.risk: The tidal-flex solution could become hand-waved arithmetic that quietly grants the submersible extra capacity or safe transits. The trapped crew could also become cargo while Illuminara solves the whole sequence from outside.

rounds.summary: The strongest opening test combines a 31-hour air clock, twenty-three trapped people, a six-seat rescue vessel and a hull rated for one transit beneath four kilometres of ocean-moon ice. It demands explicit physical reasoning and distributed human agency rather than another hidden-network or consent-protocol solution. The positive outcome is large and legible—everyone rescued—while success remains bounded by pressure, load, route and time.

Reframing adopted: the scarce resource is the sub's single hull excursion, not seats; it is spent on a hold-frame and lance, not passengers. The freed cage (rated for twelve) is the lift; the moon's flex cycle (3h14) gives eight-minute windows; Illuminara's limit is stated (eight minutes at peak, ninety seconds at trough; weight or walls, not both). Strongest rival (six seats, hull spent, seventeen left) is named in the text; cancelling observation (strain must fall by a third for five minutes at Hour 6:26) is run in scene 3. Crew choose the order and the wet-work crew; Okonkwo corrects Illuminara's picture of the collar.

This is a taut, lucid rescue story with an excellent central reframe: the scarce resource is not Curlew's six seats but its single pressure excursion, so the vessel is spent on restoring a reusable lift. Illuminara states a real limit, Maud corrects her physical picture, Imre retains certification authority, and the trapped crew choose rather than receive their rescue order. The empty-cage test, failed carriage and final erased clock create unusually clean dramatic proof. Before final, however, the draft must make the two loaded lifts fit one explicit clock, distinguish what the struts, rack, cable, flex window and Illuminara each carry, and turn Kofi's objection into a consequential decision rather than an immediately absorbed dissent.

Kept: the scarce-excursion reframe, Illuminara's stated limits (eight minutes at a peak, ninety seconds at a trough, weight or walls), Maud's correction of the picture, the east-face shear pin, Imre's single flight, Marit's refusal of lots, the empty-cage first test, the final placard. Changed: one auditable clock, one load path, a crew rule that changes the schedule. Not changed: the six-scene form, the positive outcome (all 23 reach a pressurised chamber), the dialogue format. Three changes are bundled in this revision, so any later difference cannot be attributed to one of them alone.

The revision successfully repairs the draft's three structural weaknesses without losing its taut rescue shape. Every cage leg and flex peak now sits on one absolute clock; the frame, rack, pinions, cable and Illuminara have distinct duties; and Kofi's objection creates a real one-person refusal rule that costs a full window. Imre and Maud remain indispensable, the empty-cage test still earns the mechanism, and all twenty-three people reach a chamber through bounded rather than magical competence. Before final, three small but load-bearing claims need closure: the recalculated air deadline must visibly reconcile with the opening 31-hour placard, the frame must remain independently supported and monitored after Curlew surfaces, and Kofi's decisive 2.6-to-2.2 precedent must exist in the shown evidence rather than appear only at the moment of refusal.

Narrow final pass as GPT's T04 asked, with no conceptual rewrite. Kept: the scarce-excursion reframe, stated limits, Maud's correction of the picture, the east-face pin, the single flight, Marit's refusal of lots, the empty-cage first test, the one-voice refusal rule, the final placard. Changed only: the air arithmetic (31:00 placard, 59 percent share, 46.5 h, 58:27, last window 58:10), the frame's anchoring, power and telemetry plus its cumulative cancel line, and the logged precedent that makes Kofi's refusal evidence-based. Scene 3 was split so no single speech carries both clocks. Timetable of T03 (9:40, 10:43, 11:17, 11:55, 12:50, 12:54 to 13:01:30, 17:40, 22:40, 25:50, 26:52, 29:04 planned, 32:18 actual, 37:04) is unchanged; 11:17 and 27:27 sit on the trough schedule.

Twenty-three people escape four kilometres of ice because Illuminara spends a one-use vessel on a tool rather than on six seats, states exactly where her own strength ends, and leaves the trapped crew the evidence and authority to choose the final crossing.
